correctness.rationale: Distinct conjugates: (zeta^a-zeta^b)(1-c zeta^(-a-b)) cannot vanish for distinct units since integer c and odd-order root force c=1 in any collision. The discriminant-ratio product is therefore valid. CRT counts ordered unit pairs by t=a+b locally as p^(e-1)(p-1) for p|t and p^(e-1)(p-2) otherwise; unordered pairs subtract unique diagonal exactly for primitive order m=n, explaining E_n(m). Grouping roots yields product Phi_m(c), and t=0 exponent phi(n)/2. At c=2, E_n(n)>=1 and Phi_n(2)>1; all other c !=0,2 excluded by |1-c|>1. Independent exact unit-pair enumerations for n=9,15,21,25,27,33,45,63,75 matched every exponent, but the CRT proof handles all n.
